versions.notes:
Unity Edit Tools 0.6.36 and Unity Tools Model 0.16.0.

- Model Sets has its own window: sets on the left, the chosen one on the right, and Providers and Keys as its own page. Settings › Model Sets lists the sets and opens it, as does "Manage model sets…" in Agent and Edit.
- The OpenAI API draws Edit's images. Settings › Edit offers Codex, OpenAI and OpenRouter; the OpenAI API uses your own key, kept in this computer's keychain and checked with Test without making an image.
- Arguments you keep. For the OpenAI API and OpenRouter, pick the image model from its list and set any argument it takes (quality, size or aspect ratio, images per call, seed…). A value you set is kept on every image; the rest is picked by the task's model each time. Settings › Edit has Edit's own; each Edit part of a model set has its own.

Every provider, as close to ChatGPT as it gets: Unity Tools Model 0.15.0, Agent 0.2.24, Edit 0.6.35. Ollama, LM Studio and Other go through the model bridge (Unity tools reach their models; Edit's Generate and Apply can call tools; Other takes Chat Completions too); a slow local model isn't cut off and an unloaded one is loaded with enough context; Codex's image tool works for Edit on every provider (through ChatGPT); Max and Ultra run as each API provider's most; images go at the size the model reads them; Claude in Edit caches for 5 minutes.

Model sets working well (Unity Tools Model 0.14.0, Agent 0.2.23, Edit 0.6.34). Settings › Model Sets marks a set that can't run (Needs attention), keeps half-typed text, and runs Max/Ultra efforts as Codex does now (ChatGPT as picked, Claude up to Max, API providers up to Extra high); removing a provider moves its sets to ChatGPT with ChatGPT's own model. Agent: a chat keeps its provider when its set changes or is deleted; a Claude chat on a set naming no model uses Claude Code's default; 'This chat only' no longer lists ChatGPT models for API-provider chats. Edit: reusables follow the model set. Anthropic API chats can auto-compact and no longer break on a blank reply block; refused requests read in plain words. Claude (Claude Code sign-in): Edit carries on when Claude stops early, reading files never asks, Claude Code ends with the app, plain errors.

API providers, Done (milestone V, after an independent review): Settings → Model Sets no longer marks the API providers as early releases. Ollama or LM Studio at its own address (another port or computer) is no longer refused as not running; an OpenRouter stream cut short is retried at once instead of the turn waiting 10 minutes; a context window raised after a refusal counts at once; Ollama's untagged model names and unloaded models get their real context; an OpenRouter 404 that isn't about the model keeps OpenRouter's own words. Checked with the real Codex against stand-ins of each provider; not yet run with a real API key. (Unity Tools Model 0.13.0, Agent 0.2.22, Edit 0.6.33.)

API providers, Experimental (Higher) (milestone IV, the hard cases): Ollama, LM Studio and other servers on this computer get up to 10 minutes before the first word (Codex waits 5); a server on this computer that isn't running is said before Edit's tasks too; Edit's Generate or Apply on a model that can't see images is said before the task. Every API provider is at Experimental (Higher). (Unity Tools Model 0.12.0.)

API providers, Experimental (Lower) (milestone III, spending): Claude models on OpenRouter are now cached (OpenRouter goes through the model bridge, which asks for it; Codex never did), so long chats no longer pay for the whole conversation at every step. A model OpenRouter lists as text-only gets a short note in place of each image instead of the request failing. Settings → Model Sets suggests the models your OpenRouter key can use. (Unity Tools Model 0.11.0.)

API providers, Preview (milestone II): each API provider model's real context window (OpenRouter's list, LM Studio and Ollama on this computer, an Other server's list) goes to Codex, so long chats compact before the model's limit instead of failing at it; a model with too little room for Unity Tools (under 16,384 tokens) is said before the run; the Ollama and LM Studio cards say how much context they need. Every API provider is at Preview. (Unity Tools Model 0.10.0.)

API providers, Canary (milestone I): OpenAI API, Anthropic API, DeepSeek API, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio and Other start through the same milestones Claude went through, and Settings → Model Sets shows each one's stage. About 87k fewer tokens on every request on an API provider (your ChatGPT connectors are left out of those runs). Failures on an API provider name it and what to check (key, credits, model name, limits, a server on this computer), in Korean too; Ollama or LM Studio not running is said before the turn starts. (Unity Tools Model 0.9.0, Agent 0.2.21, Edit 0.6.32.)

Claude (Claude Code sign-in), Done (milestone V): Claude matches Codex in what it can do, how it spends your plan and how it recovers. Checked on a real signed-in Claude plan: a chat with a Unity tool, Stop, and an Edit-style answer. Stop before any reply and then quitting no longer leaves a chat unable to continue; a message sent as Claude finishes is answered in that turn; Stop always ends the turn; Settings → Model Sets no longer marks Claude as an early release. (Unity Tools Model 0.8.0.)

Claude (Claude Code sign-in), Experimental (Higher): the hard cases. One window at a time per chat; Stop while an approval waits ends the turn; a message sent as Claude finishes is answered in that turn, and Stop with messages waiting never lets them run unseen; commands run where Claude Code has no sandbox (Windows, Linux without bubblewrap) instead of failing to start; 'Allow for this chat' stays in the chat; idle chats close their Claude Code after 10 minutes; a chat file that can't be written no longer ends every chat; plan limits with their reset time, an expired sign-in and a too-long conversation in plain words. Edit 0.6.31: Generate and Apply on DeepSeek, OpenRouter and other API model sets can finish (Codex gives those models no message phases, so their answer was never taken), a model that stops before its answer is asked to carry on, and Edit's own lines name the set's model instead of Codex. (Unity Tools Model 0.7.0, Agent 0.2.20, Edit 0.6.31.)

Claude (Claude Code sign-in), Experimental (Lower): your Claude plan's usage, spent as carefully as Codex spends ChatGPT's. Unity's tools load with the chat; long chats compact at about 245k tokens (the context bar measures against that); a new model or effort applies without restarting Claude Code; long Unity waits aren't cut off; chats take Claude Code's titles. Edit's parts on Claude run an empty effort at low, as on Codex. (Unity Tools Model 0.6.0, Edit 0.6.30.)

Claude (Claude Code sign-in), Preview: Setup → Claude installs, updates and signs in to Claude Code (Anthropic's installer, no administrator password). When a model set runs on Claude, a missing install or sign-in shows as something to fix and Fix Everything installs it; otherwise the rows are only offers. Claude's errors point to Setup and read in the app's language; Edit's progress for tasks on Claude says Claude. (Unity Tools Model 0.5.0, Edit 0.6.29.)

Claude (Claude Code sign-in), Canary: Edit's Generate and Apply on your Claude plan too, and Agent for people on Claude alone. Pick Claude for any part of a set in Settings → Model Sets; Edit's parts on Claude draw their images with OpenRouter (Claude can't draw), and switching a part to Claude picks your OpenRouter provider. A project on a Claude set starts Claude, not Codex; @ file search and the project's Unity Tools skills work on Claude. (Unity Tools Model 0.4.0, Agent 0.2.19, Edit 0.6.28.)

Claude (Claude Code sign-in), Initial: Agent chats on your own Claude plan. Pick Claude for a set's Agent part in Settings → Model Sets; the chat then runs on Claude Code on this computer, signed in with your Claude account, instead of Codex, with the same Unity tools, approvals, Stop, subagents and chat list. No key needed. Edit's Generate and Apply on Claude follow in a later release. (Unity Tools Model 0.3.0, Agent 0.2.18.)

Claude and DeepSeek in model sets: add the Anthropic API or DeepSeek API under Settings → Model Sets → Providers and Keys, then pick Claude or DeepSeek models per Agent chat or Edit task. Codex only speaks OpenAI's Responses API, so the app translates for them on this computer; the key never reaches Codex. Addresses are built in and model names suggested. (Unity Tools Model 0.2.0.)

Model sets: name a choice of provider, model and effort for Agent chats, Edit's Generate and Edit's Apply to Unity (Settings → Model Sets), then pick a set per Agent chat and per Edit task. A chat's subagents and the Edit tasks it starts use its set. Providers: ChatGPT sign-in, OpenAI API, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, or any Responses API address; keys stay in this computer's keychain. The starter set, Standard, works as before. (Edit 0.6.27, Agent 0.2.17, Unity Tools Model 0.1.0.)

Less Codex usage: Generate and Apply to Unity use gpt-5.6-sol · low when their model is empty (before, whatever ~/.codex/config.toml named; gpt-6-astra on the Windows PC), and long waits take one model step on Codex 0.160+ (Edit 0.6.26, Agent 0.2.16). Also includes 0.4.3: phones can open links in Agent chats.

Add Existing Project works again (it failed every time). Windows: projects open in Unity are recognized; checking for running Unity is much faster. Setup: one failing check no longer breaks the page, results refresh after a fix, a failed fix keeps its reason on the row, Codex updates work with OpenAI's standalone Codex on Windows, more reliable Windows installers, Setup in Korean. Unity Hub projects are offered until added or turned down; + menu › Add from Unity Hub…

Build fixes from an independent review: a build that fails to start no longer leaves Unity busy; a build no longer shows building forever when Unity crashes, quits or reloads; profile details no longer show Unity as closed after a build; Build To… is one-off; two quick clicks start one build; Reset also clears taught answers; Build's Unity package compiles on Unity 2021.3/2022.3 again; a reload no longer silently drops Android signing passwords. Check for Updates finds a new release at once. Bundles Unity Build Tools' Unity package 0.2.1. Includes everything in 0.4.0.

Build, finished (still experimental): plain-language fixes when a build fails (with Copy Error), 'Unity is asking' in the toolbar and sidebar, size change since the last build, Unity's full log kept for every build, Increase Build Number, works in narrow windows, fewer buttons, safer saved answers; background builds say which button Unity picked. Build from your phone (Unity Connect for Android 0.5.0 Build tab) or a terminal (unity-connect build). 한국어 everywhere: Play, the Agent chat panel and the Edit designer are translated, Korean particles follow English names. Agent's chat list works on Windows. Mac and Windows side by side: Windows recognises projects already open in Unity (no second Unity), faster Unity checks, Unity Hub projects re-offered (Add from Unity Hub… in the + menu), sturdier Setup (in Korean too), Update Codex works with Windows' standalone Codex. Higher-contrast faint text; delete confirmations focus Cancel. Bundles Unity Build Tools' Unity package 0.2.0.

Build (experimental): a new Build tab builds your game with any build profile (Unity 6 profiles or classic platforms), edits profiles (scenes, scripting defines, development build, platform settings; create, copy, rename, delete, activate), shows live progress and results (size, what takes the space, log, history), and answers Unity's questions before and during a build with the choices you set in Automatic answers. Turn it on per project in Overview › Tools in this project. Builds run in a background Unity when Unity is closed. Coming soon: install an APK on your phone through Unity Tools Connect. 한국어: the app now speaks Korean as well as English (Settings › General › Language). Menus, notifications and the app's screens are translated; the Agent chat panel and the Edit designer stay in English for now. Bundles Unity Build Tools' Unity package 0.1.0; other Unity packages unchanged.

Projects show their game's icon: each project's badge shows the app icon its active build profile would build with (the profile's own Player Settings icons when it overrides them, otherwise the project's; platform icons first, then the Default Icon). Read from the project's files, so it works whether Unity is open or closed and never starts Unity. Projects with no icon of their own keep the initials badge. Unity packages unchanged from 0.2.3.
Agent: new rules for changes Codex can make without Edit, and size and position after Apply decided case by case by quality. Bundles Edit 0.6.25.
Bundles Unity Edit Tools 0.6.24: Apply's assembly step is about 4x faster (133 s to 33 s on a 64-layer design) with byte-identical output.

Faster, steadier Agent chats. Past chats appear at once: the list is read from Codex's own chat index in a few milliseconds instead of asking Codex to scan every saved session (4-10 seconds on a long history), and it is kept between launches. Opening a chat is instant: each turn's message and answer show first, then what Codex did in the latest turn; older turns have a "Show what Codex did" row that loads on click. Large chats (Unity screenshots in tool results) no longer drop the Codex connection. Every chat request has a time limit and says what went wrong in the chat, picking chats quickly always shows the last one picked, chats keep their history after Codex stops unexpectedly, and a chat open in another Codex window (VS Code) says so. The bundled Unity Tools packages are unchanged (Base 0.1.6, Play 0.1.11, Edit 0.6.23, Debug 0.1.4).

A new look for every screen. The tools work exactly as before; only how they look and where a few controls sit changed. The window has a full-height sidebar and one toolbar with the project, the tool tabs (Overview, Play, Agent, Edit, Debug, each with its own colour), Unity's state and Open in Unity. Press ⌘K (Ctrl+K) to jump to any project or tool or run a command. Overview shows Unity's state, script errors and a tile per tool. Play's Play/Pause/Step sit in the middle like Unity's toolbar. Agent has a calmer reading column, a timeline of tool calls, clearer approval cards and suggestions on an empty chat. Edit's designer panel is grouped into cards. Debug's script editor has line numbers and C# colours, and New Session opens a small dialog. Settings has a section list and theme previews. New icons, menus, dialogs, notifications and app icon; refined light and dark themes. The bundled Unity Tools packages are unchanged (Base 0.1.6, Play 0.1.11, Edit 0.6.23, Debug 0.1.4).

UI fixes. Play: the View, Device and Zoom labels sit beside their menus again, so the rotate and pop-out buttons line up with them; the rotate buttons have proper icons; the "Connecting" box no longer repeats the sentence already shown in the empty view. Project page: the ··· menu button is visible, and in a narrow window the status line stays on one line. Edit: the empty page's New Design button has a normal + icon. A project whose folder is gone no longer shows "Checking…" forever. Opening a project no longer moves it up the project list under the pointer. The bundled Unity Tools packages are unchanged (Base 0.1.6, Play 0.1.11, Edit 0.6.23, Debug 0.1.4).

Edit: placement options from Unity Edit Tools 0.6.23. Before Codex receives a redrawn piece, Edit measures each way to place it against the design (its own fit, the visible part filling the planned box, and Codex's own numbers) and shows them side by side; Codex chooses. The bundled Edit package and project skill are 0.6.23. Fixes 0.1.0, whose placement_options tool answered with an error because its bundled toolkit lacked the options command. Not yet run in a live Apply.

First release of Unity Tools Desktop: your Unity projects with Play, Agent, Edit and Debug in one window, without VS Code. Add projects or create new ones, Unity Tools packages are installed and updated per project, Setup checks and fixes what the tools need, and the app updates itself. macOS: open the .dmg and drag the app to Applications (it isn't signed with a paid certificate yet: right-click → Open the first time). Windows: run the installer (SmartScreen may ask once).
